```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.6, dpi = 110,
  warning = FALSE
)
```

What does changing the allocation scheme change? The manual grouping of
vignette **2a** and the hierarchical cascade of **2b** raise the same discards
from the same data, with different groups of strata and different donor pools.
This vignette puts them side by side, and then varies the hierarchy itself.
It is a walkthrough, not a test: nothing here asserts pass or fail, and it is
the script to run chunk by chunk in RStudio.

* **The two schemes, raised** - each is defined in the vignette named above and
  repeated here so this one runs on its own, then raised with `catchRaising()`
  directly.
* **How much weight each raises**, and **whether each group's strata agree with
  each other**, side by side.
* **Scenarios** - a whole grouping configuration under a name, run cheaply at
  stratum level, so several hierarchies (and a manual rule set) can be lined
  up on the same strata.

It is driven directly with the vendored RDBESStockCoord functions -
`check_group_conditions()` and `catchRaising()` - the same pattern ICES's own
discard-raising scripts use. rcef's own helpers (`recommend_raising()`, and in
the scenarios `new_rule()`) do the one thing RDBESStockCoord has no opinion on
- *how* to define a group from a hierarchy or a rule set - but the raising
call they feed is the same `catchRaising()` either way.

# Data

Brill, `bll.27.3a47de`, 2025, from the CEF csv file under
`inst/extdata/data_CEF_format` (local to this machine; the file is not in the
repository). Only the catch table is needed for raising.

```{r load, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(rcef)

cef_dir <- file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", "data_CEF_format")

# blank cells (no discard domain, no trip count ...) read as NA
catch_data <- read.csv(file.path(cef_dir, "bll", "bll_2025_catches_CEF_v17.1.csv"),
                       na.strings = "")
```

```{r derive}
catch_data <- derive_fields(x = catch_data)
```

## The stratum resolution

`dims` is the set of columns that defines a stratum for the hierarchical
scheme and for the comparison below. Its columns are the same, in the same
order, as the hierarchy - `stratum_id` is `paste(dims values, sep = " | ")`,
which is order-sensitive, so two different orders would build two different
ids for the same stratum and every `stratum_id %in% c(...)` condition would
silently match nothing.

`stratum_id`, `coverage`, `discard_rate`, `n_measurements` and `numTrips` are
added onto `catch_data` itself, once, here - not a second table kept
alongside it. Only the hierarchical scheme reads them, but they are harmless
extra columns for the manual scheme's plain `metier4` / `catchCategory` /
`fleetValue` conditions, so one `catch_data` serves both.

```{r dims}
dims <- c("Country", "Season", "mesh", "metier4")
catch_data <- add_stratum_metrics(data = catch_data, dims = dims)
```

# The two schemes, raised

## Manual (2a)

The same six groups as the RDBESStockCoord example this is based on: G1-G3
split the main gears, G4 is a REST group for everything else, G5 pulls out
the incidental-bycatch (IBC) `fleetValue` sentinel, G6 is BMS on its own -
between them every row is claimed exactly once. G4 draws its rate on every
gear, minus five strata whose own discard ratio the source example flagged as
implausible. See vignette 2a for the reasoning per group.

```{r manual}
strataCond_manual <- list(
  G1 = quo(metier4 == "TBB" & catchCategory != "BMS"),
  G2 = quo(metier4 %in% c("GTR", "GNS") & catchCategory != "BMS"),
  G3 = quo(metier4 %in% c("OTB", "SSC", "SDN") & catchCategory != "BMS"),
  G4 = quo(!metier4 %in% c("TBB", "GTR", "GNS", "OTB", "SSC", "SDN") &
             catchCategory != "BMS" & fleetValue != "MIS_MIS_0_0_0_IBC"),
  G5 = quo(fleetValue == "MIS_MIS_0_0_0_IBC" & catchCategory != "BMS"),
  G6 = quo(catchCategory == "BMS"))

matchedDataCond_manual <- list(
  G1 = strataCond_manual$G1,
  G2 = strataCond_manual$G2,
  G3 = strataCond_manual$G3,
  G4 = quo(catchCategory != "BMS" &
             fleetValue != "MIS_MIS_0_0_0_IBC" &
             !((vesselFlagCountry == "Sweden" & areaValue == "27.3.a.21" &
                  fleetValue == "GNS_DEF_all_0_0_all" & seasonValue %in% c(2, 3)) |
                 (vesselFlagCountry == "Sweden" & areaValue == "27.3.a.21" &
                    fleetValue == "GTR_DEF_all_0_0_all" & seasonValue %in% c(2, 4)) |
                 (vesselFlagCountry == "France" & areaValue == "27.7.e" &
                    fleetValue == "GTR_DEF_100-119_0_0_all" & seasonValue == 2) |
                 (vesselFlagCountry == "Sweden" & areaValue == "27.3.a.21" &
                    fleetValue == "OTB_CRU_90-119_0_0_all" & seasonValue == 3) |
                 (vesselFlagCountry == "Sweden" & areaValue == "27.3.a.21" &
                    fleetValue == "OTB_CRU_70-89_2_35_all" & seasonValue == 1))),
  G5 = strataCond_manual$G5,
  G6 = strataCond_manual$G6)
```

The condition diagnostics - every stratum claimed exactly once - and the
raise itself. The engine prints a "Condition diagnostics" banner for each
condition; it is hidden here.

```{r manual-raise, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
cond_st <- check_group_conditions(catch_data = catch_data,
                                  condition_list = strataCond_manual,
                                  domain = "domainCatchDis",
                                  originType = "WGEstimate",
                                  variableType = "WeightLive",
                                  logFile = NULL, append = TRUE)
cond_md <- check_group_conditions(catch_data = catch_data,
                                  condition_list = matchedDataCond_manual,
                                  conditionType = "matched_data",
                                  domain = "domainCatchDis",
                                  originType = "WGEstimate",
                                  variableType = "WeightLive",
                                  logFile = NULL, append = TRUE)

raised_manual <- catchRaising(catch_data = catch_data,
                              condition_raising_st_list = strataCond_manual,
                              condition_matched_data_list = matchedDataCond_manual,
                              type = "discards",
                              originType = "WGEstimate",
                              variableType = "WeightLive",
                              logFile = file.path(tempdir(), "raising_log.txt"))
```

```{r manual-result}
strata_matrix <- do.call(cbind, cond_st)
cat(sprintf("manual: %d rows in no group, %d rows in more than one (both should be 0)\n",
            sum(rowSums(strata_matrix) == 0), sum(rowSums(strata_matrix) > 1)))
cat(sprintf("manual raising: %d rows (%d imported, %d raised)\n",
            nrow(raised_manual),
            sum(raised_manual$importedOrRaised == "imported"),
            sum(raised_manual$importedOrRaised == "raised")))
```

## Hierarchical (2b)

`recommend_raising()` cascades from the stratum's own data outward: own
stratum, then join countries, then seasons, then mesh, then `metier4` alone,
then everything - each level with its own coverage bar. `conds_from_auto()`
turns the recommendation into the same `strataCond` / `matchedDataCond` shape
as the manual scheme. See vignette 2b for the cascade step by step.

```{r hier}
hierarchy  <- c("Country", "Season", "mesh", "metier4")
thresholds <- 50

rec <- recommend_raising(strata = catch_data, hierarchy = hierarchy,
                         thresholds = thresholds)
auto_conds <- conds_from_auto(rec = rec)
nrow(auto_conds$groups)   # groups
```

```{r hier-raise, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
cond_st_h <- check_group_conditions(catch_data = catch_data,
                                    condition_list = auto_conds$strataCond,
                                    domain = "domainCatchDis",
                                    originType = "WGEstimate",
                                    variableType = "WeightLive",
                                    logFile = NULL, append = TRUE)
cond_md_h <- check_group_conditions(catch_data = catch_data,
                                    condition_list = auto_conds$matchedDataCond,
                                    conditionType = "matched_data",
                                    domain = "domainCatchDis",
                                    originType = "WGEstimate",
                                    variableType = "WeightLive",
                                    logFile = NULL, append = TRUE)

raised_hier <- catchRaising(catch_data = catch_data,
                            condition_raising_st_list = auto_conds$strataCond,
                            condition_matched_data_list = auto_conds$matchedDataCond,
                            type = "discards",
                            originType = "WGEstimate",
                            variableType = "WeightLive",
                            logFile = file.path(tempdir(), "raising_log.txt"))
```

```{r hier-result}
strata_matrix_h <- do.call(cbind, cond_st_h)
cat(sprintf("hierarchical: %d rows in no group, %d rows in more than one (both should be 0)\n",
            sum(rowSums(strata_matrix_h) == 0), sum(rowSums(strata_matrix_h) > 1)))
cat(sprintf("hierarchical raising: %d rows (%d imported, %d raised)\n",
            nrow(raised_hier),
            sum(raised_hier$importedOrRaised == "imported"),
            sum(raised_hier$importedOrRaised == "raised")))
```

# How much weight each scheme raises

Imported against raised, at any aggregation, shown for both schemes so the
same weight can be compared scheme to scheme. `plot_raised_catches()`
takes any catch-side column on `x` and an optional `facet`: landings /
discards are always the fill, imported / raised is always the shading, and
whatever you put on `x` or `facet` is the aggregation.

```{r overview-table-manual}
raised_overview_table(raised = raised_manual)
```

```{r overview-table-hier}
raised_overview_table(raised = raised_hier)
```

The bottom line side by side: the total discards each scheme ends up with
(imported + raised, tonnes), and how many raised rows came out as `NaN` -
a group with no donor to draw a rate from raises to nothing, and those rows
are left out of the sum (see the last section of 2a and 2b).

```{r bottom-line}
schemes <- list(manual = raised_manual, hierarchical = raised_hier)
data.frame(
  discards_t = vapply(schemes, function(r)
    round(sum(r$total[r$catchCategory == "Dis"], na.rm = TRUE) / 1000, 2), 0),
  raised_rows = vapply(schemes, function(r) sum(r$importedOrRaised == "raised"), 0L),
  nan_rows = vapply(schemes, function(r) sum(is.nan(r$total)), 0L))
```

By metier, one scheme after the other:

```{r overview-metier-manual, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Manual scheme: imported and raised weight by metier"}
plot_raised_catches(raised_catch = raised_manual, x = "metier4")
```

```{r overview-metier-hier, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Hierarchical scheme: imported and raised weight by metier"}
plot_raised_catches(raised_catch = raised_hier, x = "metier4")
```

By country, faceted by season - a finer aggregation than the group
definitions themselves ever used:

```{r overview-country-manual, fig.height = 6.5, fig.alt = "Manual scheme: imported and raised weight by country, one panel per season"}
plot_raised_catches(raised_catch = raised_manual, x = "Country", facet = "Season")
```

```{r overview-country-hier, fig.height = 6.5, fig.alt = "Hierarchical scheme: imported and raised weight by country, one panel per season"}
plot_raised_catches(raised_catch = raised_hier, x = "Country", facet = "Season")
```

# Do the groups agree with themselves?

A different question from how much weight moved: whether the *strata a group
draws its rate from* agree with each other. `plot_raised_DR()` puts the
raising **group** on `x` and shows one point per donor stratum, muted,
underneath the raised catch's own points - a group whose donor cloud is
scattered from 2% to 40% is not a group, it is a guess, no matter how
plausible its own raised rate looks on top.

## Manual

`plot_raised_DR()` re-tests `matchedDataCond_manual` against `catch_data`
internally (the same "per-stratum spread behind each group average" check the
source example runs before raising) and plots one point per donor stratum,
muted, underneath the raised catch's own points. The table's `rate` is
discards / covered landings - the source example's `dis_ratio` and the CAS
output's `rate`.

```{r donors-manual-plot, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Discard rate of the manual scheme's raised catch and its donor strata, coloured by metier"}
plot_raised_DR(raised_catch = raised_manual, catch_data = catch_data,
              matched_data_cond = matchedDataCond_manual,
              x = "DrGroup", colour = "metier4")
```

## Hierarchical

Here too the donors of a group are *not* the strata it raises: a stratum
raised from a wide pool often has no discard data of its own, and the pool a
group draws on is every stratum sharing its key values - `auto_conds$matchedDataCond`,
not `auto_conds$strataCond`.

```{r donors-hier-plot, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5.5, fig.alt = "Discard rate of the hierarchical scheme's raised catch and its donor strata, coloured by metier"}
plot_raised_DR(raised_catch = raised_hier, catch_data = catch_data,
              matched_data_cond = auto_conds$matchedDataCond,
              x = "DrGroup", colour = "metier4")
```

# Scenarios: what the hierarchy's shape changes

A **scenario** is a whole grouping configuration under a name.
`scenario_auto()` and `scenario_manual()` describe one, `run_scenario()` runs
it end to end - build the strata, define the groups, apply the raising - with
the light *stratum-level* raising `apply_raising()` does, not the full
CEF-row `catchRaising()` run above, which is what makes running several of
them cheap enough to compare. `compare_scenarios()` lines the runs up on the
same stratum keys; `plot_comparison()` draws them.

The threshold policy is held **fixed** (50% at every level, the own-stratum
bar included) and only the hierarchy itself varies - which keys get pooled
over, in what order. The first key listed is pooled over soonest and the last
one kept longest: `c("Country", "metier4")` means "join countries first, then
`metier4` alone"; `c("Country", "areaValue", "metier4")` means "join
countries, then areas, then `metier4` alone". Every variant keeps `metier4` as
the last, most-protected key except the first, which considers it alone from
the start.

`scenario_auto()`'s own `dims` can be *wider* than the shared comparison
`dims` (the Country > area > `metier4` variant needs `areaValue` in its own
strata) but never narrower: `compare_scenarios()` re-aggregates every run onto
the fixed `dims` keys, so a run missing any one of them on its own output
would fail right there.

`scenario_manual()` takes rules in `new_rule()` shape - the one place these
vignettes use `new_rule()`, only because that is the input this particular
comparison function needs. It runs at `build_strata()`'s resolution, where
`catchCategory` has already been summed away into landings and discards and
`fleetValue` no longer exists - so the manual scheme's BMS / IBC groups and
G4's hand-picked exclusion have no equivalent here. This is the closest
structural analogue at that resolution: the same G1-G3 gear split, with a
plain catch-all in place of G4-G6 (a `new_rule()` with no clause claims
whatever is left).

```{r scenarios}
manual_rules <- list(
  new_rule(id = "G1", label = "TBB",
           raise = list(list(var = "metier4", values = "TBB", negate = FALSE))),
  new_rule(id = "G2", label = "GTR / GNS",
           raise = list(list(var = "metier4", values = c("GTR", "GNS"),
                             negate = FALSE))),
  new_rule(id = "G3", label = "OTB / SSC / SDN",
           raise = list(list(var = "metier4", values = c("OTB", "SSC", "SDN"),
                             negate = FALSE))),
  new_rule(id = "G4", label = "Rest of the gears"))

dims_area <- c(dims, "areaValue")    # only the Country > area > metier4 variant needs it

scenarios <- list(
  manual_used = scenario_manual(name = "Manual (gear split)", dims = dims,
                                rules = manual_rules, sets = list()),
  hier_used   = scenario_auto(name = "Country > Season > mesh > metier4 (the 2b cascade)",
                              dims = dims, hierarchy = hierarchy, thresholds = thresholds,
                              self_threshold = thresholds[1]),
  hier_metier_only            = scenario_auto(name = "metier4 only", dims = dims,
                                              hierarchy = "metier4", thresholds = 50,
                                              self_threshold = 50),
  hier_country_metier         = scenario_auto(name = "Country > metier4", dims = dims,
                                              hierarchy = c("Country", "metier4"),
                                              thresholds = c(50, 50),
                                              self_threshold = 50),
  hier_country_season_metier  = scenario_auto(name = "Country > Season > metier4", dims = dims,
                                              hierarchy = c("Country", "Season", "metier4"),
                                              thresholds = c(50, 50, 50), self_threshold = 50),
  hier_country_area_metier    = scenario_auto(name = "Country > area > metier4", dims = dims_area,
                                              hierarchy = c("Country", "areaValue", "metier4"),
                                              thresholds = c(50, 50, 50), self_threshold = 50))

runs <- lapply(scenarios, run_scenario, catch_data = catch_data)
cmp  <- compare_scenarios(runs = runs, dims = dims)
```

## One stratum, every scenario

The wide table: one row per stratum, one column per scenario's estimated
discards (plus what was imported), so a single stratum's answer can be read
straight across - the biggest strata first.

```{r comparison-table}
ct <- comparison_table(cmp = cmp, keys = dims)
val_cols <- setdiff(names(ct), dims)
head(ct[order(-rowSums(ct[val_cols], na.rm = TRUE)), ], 10)
```

## The scenarios drawn

```{r comparison-metier, fig.alt = "Estimated discards by metier, one bar group per scenario"}
plot_comparison(cmp = cmp, x_var = "metier4")
```

```{r comparison-country, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 8, fig.alt = "Estimated discards by country, one panel per metier, one bar group per scenario"}
plot_comparison(cmp = cmp, x_var = "Country", facet_var = "metier4")
```
